scenarios.name: cross-language-fingerprint-identity
scenarios.description: Identical semantic structures from EN/EL source texts produce the same fingerprint

scenarios.name: cross-language-retrieval
scenarios.description: Store preference in English, retrieve with identical sem — should find exact match

scenarios.name: constraint-modality-separation
scenarios.description: Obligation vs permission constraints have distinct fingerprints and both store correctly

scenarios.name: preference-override-detection
scenarios.description: Old and new preference share structure but differ in content — detectable as override

scenarios.name: multilingual-canonical-equivalence
scenarios.description: Same sem from 4 languages (EN/EL/ES/JA) produces identical fingerprint

scenarios.name: conditional-preferences
scenarios.description: Conditional clauses survive the full create→canonicalize→compare cycle

scenarios.name: negated-constraints
scenarios.description: Negated obligation constraints preserve negation flag through the pipeline

scenarios.name: multi-constraint-entry
scenarios.description: Multiple constraints in one entry all survive the pipeline

scenarios.name: user-correction-flow
scenarios.description: After storing a correction, both old and new are retrievable — agent can detect the override

successCriteria: Multilingual source texts map to same canonical sem
rollbackCriteria: Modality or negation lost through pipeline
